hook: You are not a victim of fate; you are merely refusing to love it.
concept: Amor Fati: The radical embrace of everything that happens, not merely tolerating it, but actively willing it.
stoics: Marcus Aurelius — Emperor who wrote his personal philosophical journal, Meditations, amidst war and plague.
Seneca the Younger — Advisor to Nero, forced to commit suicide, who wrote extensively on death and adversity.
Epictetus — Former slave who founded his own school, teaching the power of internal control.

passos.titulo: Step one. Distinguish the event from your judgment of it.
passos.foco: Practicing objective perception of facts, stripped of emotional labels.

passos.titulo: Step two. Accept the unchangeable nature of what has transpired.
passos.foco: Meditating on the past as a fixed, irreversible part of the cosmic order.

passos.titulo: Step three. Identify the hidden lessons or strengths adversity offers.
passos.foco: Journaling about how challenges can build resilience and character.

passos.titulo: Step four. Reframe the event as an integral piece of your unique path.
passos.foco: Consciously narrating the event as essential to your personal development.

passos.titulo: Step five. Actively integrate the past into your present self.
passos.foco: Reflecting on how all past experiences, good or bad, form who you are now.

passos.titulo: Step six. Proactively prepare your mind for future difficulties.
passos.foco: Engaging in premeditatio malorum, mentally rehearsing future challenges.
